title: OPSRL-SSP: Optimistic Posterior Sampling for Stochastic Shortest Path with Minimax-Optimal Regret
claim: Our method achieves low, sublinear cumulative regret competitive with the best baselines, while several other approaches grow far faster.
layout: 2 side-by-side line plots, shared legend style, shaded confidence bands
description: Two side-by-side line charts plot cumulative regret against episode count, from 0 to 5,000. The left panel is titled RandomMDP, with a y-axis up to 800. The right panel is titled GridWorld, with a y-axis up to 300,000. Each panel has a legend in the upper right listing nine algorithms: Q-learning, LCB-ADVANTAGE-SSP, UC-SSP, Bernstein-SSP, ULCVI, EB-SSP, SVI-SSP, PSRL-SSP and OPSRL-SSP. OPSRL-SSP is drawn in olive. In RandomMDP, Q-learning rises almost linearly to about 770 and LCB-ADVANTAGE-SSP reaches about 430. The other methods flatten out at roughly 100 to 150. In GridWorld, LCB-ADVANTAGE-SSP climbs steeply to about 280,000, Q-learning to about 240,000 and Bernstein-SSP to about 120,000. The remaining methods stay below about 50,000. Faint shaded bands show 95% confidence intervals. The eye goes first to the steep blue and orange curves.
caption: Cumulative regret of SSP algorithms on RandomMDP (left) and GridWorld (right) over 5,000 episodes. Curves are averaged over 500 runs; shaded areas show 95% confidence intervals.
abstract: We study online reinforcement learning for the stochastic shortest path (SSP) problem with unknown transition dynamics. Although existing posterior-sampling methods perform well empirically on SSPs, their regret guarantees do not achieve the minimax-optimal order. We address this limitation by proposing OPSRL-SSP, an optimistic posterior-sampling algorithm for the SSP setting. The algorithm operates in epochs and uses a logarithmic, time-dependent schedule for the number of posterior samples. To induce optimism, we augment the transition model with a pseudo-state assigned an optimistic boundary value. We establish a high-probability regret bound of $\tilde{O}(B_\star \sqrt{SAK} + B_\star S^2 A)$, where $B_\star$ is an upper bound on the expected cost of the optimal policy, $S$ and $A$ are the numbers of states and actions, respectively, and $K$ is the number of episodes. In addition, we extend the analysis to general zero-cost SSPs using a universal cost-perturbation argument. The leading term matches the minimax lower bound $Î©(B_\star \sqrt{SAK})$, thereby addressing the open problem raised by Jafarnia-Jahromi et al. [19] for posterior sampling in the SSP setting.
